subject.title: feat: Tiered bootstrap file loading for progressive context control

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and if so what defaults and hook-extra semantics should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/22439 use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing a new config/default surface affects prompt context, session behavior, upgrade expectations, hook extras, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals in a way automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor The Linked PR Shape
options.body: Proceed with maintainer review of the linked PR as the focused additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Bootstrap Selection
options.body: Pause this focused request behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46565 and design one public selector contract covering tiering, per-session filtering, and related prompt-pressure work together.

options.title: Decline A New Config Knob
options.body: Keep the current fixed filters and steer users toward existing `contextInjection`, budget, lightweight-mode, or doctor guidance instead of adding `bootstrapTier`.

recommendation.title: Sponsor The Linked PR Shape
recommendation.body: Proceed with maintainer review of the linked PR as the focused additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.
